exposure: Dawes-Redman algorithm output (criteria met/not met) from antepartum fetal heart rate traces
outcome: Adverse pregnancy outcome (APO, defined as at least one of seven adverse neonatal outcomes after delivery)
cohort: The study included term singleton pregnancies (37+0 to 41+6 weeks' gestation) whose antepartum fetal heart rate traces were obtained between 1991 and 2024.
finding: The Dawes-Redman algorithm effectively identifies fetal wellbeing with high specificity (90.7%) but has limitations in identifying fetuses at risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes due to low sensitivity (18.2%).
followup_time: Outcomes were assessed at or immediately after birth, based on FHR traces taken up to 48 hours prior to delivery.
